Title: Server-side Sanity-curated retailer filter for Shopping List Serper search
Description: Make the server-side Serper search restrict results to the active retailers Anahit curates in Sanity, instead of relying only on Googles gl= geo-targeting which returns ANY UK-shipping shop. Today (post I-026): Sanity holds the curated catalog but only feeds the frontend logo strip — the server still passes country code to Serper unfiltered, so Google decides what shops appear. Result: market-research effort to curate UK/US/etc. retailers in Sanity is wasted on the actual search. FIX: server fetches active retailers from Sanity at boot (cached ~5 min in-memory, refresh on cache miss), maps country code (us/gb/ca/...) → Sanity region tag (US/UK/Canada/...), filters retailers where regions includes that tag + active=true, builds a Serper  filter and appends to each search query. Fallback to retailers.ts bundled list if Sanity unreachable (same pattern as ProjectsContext fromSanity flag). DEPENDENCY: bundle with the UK activation work currently in flight — UK enablement is misleading without this (user picks UK, gets Google-curated UK shops, not Anahits curated UK list).
Why: Owner curated retailer lists per region (US live, UK newly added) in Sanity specifically to drive the Shopping List search. Without server-side reading from Sanity, the curation effort and market research only affects the visible logo strip — not the actual products users see. This closes the loop on I-026: Sanity edits = browser-editable catalog = search results that reflect the catalog.
Status: Idea (bundling with in-flight UK activation PR)
Notes: Owner-initiated 2026-06-25 after gap surfaced during the UK activation impl session: discovered Serper gl=gb only does geo-targeting, not retailer restriction. Recommendation: bundle with the in-flight UK PR rather than separate ticket — UK enablement without curated-search is misleading UX. Server fetches active Sanity retailers, builds  filter from their domains, applies to Serper query. ~2-3h impl. Same fallback pattern as ProjectsContext (retailers.ts bundled list when Sanity unreachable). Test: select UK, search for chair, confirm results domains are subset of UK retailers in Sanity.

Title: AI Vision — Persist generated concepts across page reload until logout

Why: Owner feedback 2026-05-22 while debugging AI-030: 'when something is reloaded nothing is preserved from previous login… if the person is still inside the concept even the free user does not have a dashboard it should keep the session active until it logs out.' Cap stored size (data URLs can be ~1MB each; sessionStorage limit is typically 5MB per origin — store ~3 concepts max + the source room + the inspirations). Title: Fix duplicate SPF records on designature.studio
Description: Two competing TXT records at apex: 'v=spf1 redirect=_spf.mail.ru' AND 'v=spf1 +a +mx include:spf.mysecurecloudhost...'. Per RFC 7208 a domain may have only one SPF record — having two causes receiving mail servers to fail SPF auth (permerror), which routes legitimate mail to spam. Fix: keep ONE record, with the right include for whichever provider actually sends mail. If Mail.ru is the active provider, drop the mysecurecloudhost SPF; if hosting.com mail is active, drop the Mail.ru redirect.
Why: Email deliverability from @designature.studio is at risk. Priority depends on whether the domain actually sends/receives email today.
Notes: Confirm with owner which mail provider is active. Renumbered I-006 → I-035 on 2026-09-05 (duplicate-ID cleanup; canonical I-006 = 'Env path fallback' (row 87), referenced in CLAUDE.md + memory).

Title: Testimonials shuffle bug — biased Math.random sort + reduce visible from 4 to 3
Description: Bug + small UX tightening on the home-page Testimonials section. (1) BIAS BUG: src/components/Testimonials.tsx:29 uses `[...data.testimonials].sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5)` to shuffle — this is the well-known biased-shuffle anti-pattern (Array.sort comparators must return -1/0/1 deterministically; using a random sign produces a statistically biased order where earlier-indexed items tend to stay earlier). Replace with a proper Fisher-Yates shuffle: iterate from end, swap each element with a random earlier (or same) index. (2) PAGE_SIZE: change const PAGE_SIZE = 4 → 3. (3) GRID: change `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` → `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (line ~68 + ~74) so the layout matches 3 cards on desktop. (4) Pagination math (pageCount, prev/next, page indicator) keeps working unchanged — derived from `Math.ceil(all.length / PAGE_SIZE)` which auto-adjusts (10 testimonials / 3 per page = 4 pages instead of 3, which actually makes ALL testimonials reachable via pagination — currently with 10/4 = 3 pages, the last page has 2 cards which is a layout gap anyway).
Why: Owner verified 2026-05-31: 10 testimonials in the Sheet all approved, but reloading the home page shows nearly the same 4 testimonials each time. Root cause = the biased sort. Plus owner wants 3 visible at a time (not 4) for cleaner grid + faster perceived rotation. Visible quality issue — testimonials are social proof at the top of the conversion funnel.
Status: Dropped - live Voices.tsx does not shuffle
Notes:
Tiny fix — single file (src/components/Testimonials.tsx), ~15 LOC change, ~20 min impl + verify. No backend changes; server-side caching (10-min TESTIMONIALS_CACHE_MS) and Apps Script pipeline both unchanged. The client-side shuffle runs on every component mount, so a fixed Fisher-Yates means each page reload genuinely re-randomises which 3 of N appear first. Owner dispatching impl immediately — corresponding impl prompt in chat.

Title: GA4 custom events — calendly_open, signup, ai_generate, quota_burned, newsletter_signup
Description: I-007 wired gtag.js for page_view only. I-022 added SPA page_view per route. The five high-intent user actions still aren't measurable in GA4: (1) calendly_open — fired today from src/lib/track.ts trackCalendly() which only POSTs to /api/track/calendly internal log, not to GA4; (2) signup — fires today via internal /api/track endpoints but not GA4; (3) ai_generate — when user generates an AI Vision concept (consumes a quota); (4) quota_burned — when free user hits 0 remaining concepts (key conversion signal); (5) newsletter_signup — from the offline-Shopping card and footer. For each, add a gtag('event', '<name>', { ...params }) call alongside the existing internal tracker so both systems see the same events. Suggested params: calendly_open { source }, signup { method: 'google' }, ai_generate { tool, style }, quota_burned { tool }, newsletter_signup { source }. Tiny per-event diff. After ship: GA4 conversions report becomes usable; can build funnels in GA4 Explore.
Why: Without custom events GA4 is page-view-only — usable for SEO/traffic but blind to the actual product funnel (visit → quiz → vision generate → quota hit → calendly call). Quota_burned in particular is the most important conversion signal we have for the Free → Paid story; not capturing it is a gap.
Notes: SHIPPED 2026-05-29 in one combined PR with A-004 + A-005 (PR #30, squash b62b779). All 5 events wired via trackEvent() helper in src/lib/analytics.ts alongside existing internal /api/track/* calls (untouched): calendly_open {source} at 7 CTA sites (counted under A-005), signup {source} (added isNewUser field to /api/auth/google response so client knows to fire), ai_generate covered by the 8 ai_* events under A-004, newsletter_signup {source} (Footer + ShoppingOfflineCard + ShoppingListShowcase success handlers), quota_burned {tool} fires when a generate response leaves the user at 0 remaining. 13-event registry doc-comment at top of analytics.ts. Title: AI Studio onboarding diagnostic — "Where do I start?"
Description: A visitor lands on /ai-studio, sees 16 cards across 5 phases, and has no idea which is theirs. Four chip questions (where are you in the project · what is actually stopping you · one room or whole home · what do you need to walk away with) return a PERSONAL ORDERED WORKFLOW of 3-5 tools instead of a menu. Deliberately NOT an AI feature - a deterministic weights table, zero model calls: instant, free, unit-testable, and it can never invent a tool we do not have. Score selects, phase orders (Discover-Plan-Visualize-Specify-Realize) so the path always reads as a journey; the tool answering the blocker question is marked "this is your actual problem". Includes an HONEST EXIT - mid-renovation + whole home + builder-ready returns no path at all, just the free 15-min call. Guests take it without an account; resumable with a "Step 2 of 4" progress strip.
Why: Raises the value of every tool already built, which no 11th tool can do. Six tools exist and ten more are planned - adding another card to a screen nobody can navigate does not increase usage. Also answers a question the studio cannot currently answer at all: what do visitors actually believe their problem is? (Q2's distribution feeds GEO phrase selection.)
Dependencies: AI-021 (Done - explorer rail/panel already in production)
Notes: SPEC: _Plan/Website/AI-032-AI-Studio-Onboarding-Flow.md · MOCKUP: _Mockups/Website/WEBSITE-PLAN-AI032-studio-onboarding-flow.html. Requested by owner 2026-08-24. 5-7 ideal days across 4 phases. New src/data/studioRouter.ts = single source of truth for the weights table. No AI, no new vendor, no new infrastructure.

Title: AI Vision — accept a floorplan as input (the Plan My Room bridge)
Description: Today AI Vision receives a photo and must ESTIMATE the room (spatialAnalysis.ts) - that estimate is the root of every structure-preservation bug and of AI-029. Arriving from Plan My Room there is nothing to estimate. TWO BRANCHES, one tool: (A) FROM THE PLAN - geometry + camera pin + style, photo optional, structure known, renders the planned room exactly; (B) DIRECT LANDING - photo + style, structure estimated, today's behaviour unchanged, with an upsell to Plan My Room. Level 1: geometry -> a precise scene brief + camera, into the existing Gemini call. Level 2: project the room and furniture as plain blocks from the camera, render a line/depth map, use as ControlNet conditioning - AI-029 Phase 3 with an EXACT depth map. Branch A also unlocks rendering with NO photo at all: empty apartments, gut renovations, new builds.
Why: Turns the floorplan from a sibling tool into an upgrade path for the tool we already monetise, and fixes the AI-029 class of bugs at source rather than by prompt-nudging. Branch A serves a customer Vision cannot serve today.
Notes: Raised by owner 2026-08-25 reviewing AI-016; two-branch model added 2026-08-26 on owner call. Spec: _Plan/Website/AI-016-Floorplan-Generator-Plan.md sheet 09. Camera contract = the user taps where they stood on their own plan and drags to aim (deriving it from the photo is brittle; EXIF gives heading at best, never position). STYLE IS REQUIRED - via preset chip, Style Quiz profile or an uploaded reference image. Revives D6: 3D returns as plumbing (~1 day for a box projection).

Title: Heat My Room — heating & cooling plan
Description: Radiators, baseboards, HVAC supply registers and returns, AC units, underfloor heating. Deliberately split OUT of AI-016 on 2026-08-25: the floorplan generator is about furniture placement, and once you draw a radiator you owe the user the AC, the vents and the returns too. Consumes the same geometry model AI-016 produces.
Why: Keeps the floorplan generator honest and shippable. Heating is a real deliverable but a different discipline with its own rulebook.
Notes: Owner call 2026-08-25: 'if radiator is there we must have ac, and other heating/cooling stuff'. Radiator and floor-register symbols removed from the AI-016 library at the same time; R9 narrowed to service ACCESS only. A fireplace stays in AI-016 - not as heating, but because it is often the real anchor of a US living room (R16).

Title: Plumb My Room — wet-services plan (sanitary, drainage, supply)
Description: Sanitary fixtures, drainage falls and stack positions, hot/cold supply runs and shut-offs, for kitchens and bathrooms — the wet-services layer of the plan. Consumes the same geometry model as AI-016 and AI-034. Identified 2026-08-27 while drawing the AI-032 v2 scenario routes: the roster already carries Light My Room (AI-011), Wire My Room (AI-018) and Heat My Room (AI-034) between Redesign and Shop, but there is nothing at all for water.
Why: No kitchen or bathroom route can complete without it, and those are the two highest-spend rooms in any home. Drainage falls and stack positions decide a wet-room layout before anything aesthetic does — a render that ignores them is a convincing picture of a room nobody can build.
Notes: Proposed 2026-08-27 from the AI-032 v2 scenario route map (_Plan\Website\AI-032v2-Scenario-Pipelines.md). Sits on 2 of the 11 visitor routes (mid-renovation, wet room) — few routes, but the priciest rooms. Also needs a card added to src/components/studio/explorerRoster.ts.

Title: Schedule My Finishes — room-by-room finishes schedule with quantities
Description: Turns a concept into quantities: m2 of tile and flooring, litres of paint, linear metres of skirting and trim, per room, as a takeoff a supplier can actually price. Shop My Room finds PRODUCTS; it cannot quantify MATERIALS, and nothing else on the board does either.
Why: The card that makes Shop My Room useful to a renovator rather than a decorator. Without it Shop can only ever buy furniture — which is exactly where a renovating visitor hits the wall today. Highest-frequency unbuilt card on the AI-032 v2 route map: 4 of 11 routes run through it.
Notes: Proposed 2026-08-27 from the AI-032 v2 scenario route map. Build-order argument there puts it second, after AI-012 Cost My Project. Build My Moodboard (AI-014) is arguably a step INSIDE this card rather than a card of its own — decide that before building either. Also needs a card in explorerRoster.ts.

Title: Virtual-staging engine (fal FLUX) — re-test vs Gemini before activating
Description: The fal.ai FLUX apartment-staging engine (img2img — keeps the real room, only adds furniture, so it structurally cannot invent windows/doors) is built in services/aiVision/virtualStaging.ts and wired into generateConcept.ts, but opt-in only (AI_VISION_ENGINE=staging + FAL_KEY). Default = improved Gemini.
Why: Gemini occasionally distorts room structure (widens walls, invents/moves windows). fal cannot — so if structure drift ever becomes the bigger problem, fal is the built-in safety option worth reactivating.
Notes: Owner raised 2026-08-28. A prior session tested fal, found it 'not working at all', Gemini 'way better', kept it dormant. Needs FAL_KEY + credits (~$0.02/img). Re-test = run the SAME empty room through fal vs Gemini side by side, owner picks, THEN decide default. Do NOT activate blind.

Title: Pipeline-driven engagement app — push notifications + full site parity
Description: Native mobile app (iOS + Android) — or a PWA-first phase — that ships feature parity with designature.studio AND adds pipeline-aware push notifications. When a visitor picks a scenario in the AI Studio onboarding (AI-032 / AI-032v2), the app treats that scenario as an ordered pipeline through specific cards. As the user completes a card (or when time gates expire), a push nudges them to the next stage — "Nice, your palette is locked. Ready to see it? → Redesign My Room" — turning what is today a website into a coached, months-long journey. Feature parity is non-negotiable: everything the site does today (AI Vision, Shopping List, Room Audit, Style Quiz, /account library, /consultation booking) works inside the app.
Why: The website is transactional — visit, do a tool, leave. A design project is a month-long journey with many stages. Push notifications are the only reliable channel to bring a user back at the RIGHT moment for the NEXT stage of THEIR pipeline. Also protects retention against generic AI chatbots that lack a personal journey model.
Dependencies: AI-032, AI-032v2, AC-001 (dashboard), I-030 (paid tiers), M-002 (native app stack)
Notes: Owner 2026-08-30. Complements — not replaces — M-002. M-002 is the "native apps exist at all" question; M-003 is the specific product feature that would justify building them (or a PWA phase first). Two possible technical paths: (1) PWA with web push — ships fast, no app stores, works everywhere but iOS Safari push has caveats; (2) React Native or Expo native app — reuses most React code, real push notifications, app-store presence. Recommend Phase 1 = PWA, Phase 2 = native. Depends on AI-032v2 being live in the site first (the pipeline definition is the substrate the notifications ride on). 2026-09-06 decision: phase 1 is M-004 (installable app plus push), scheduled for 2026-09-28 to 2026-11-08. M-003 keeps the pipeline aware nudges, which need AI-032 v2 live first and ride on the push plumbing M-004 builds.

Title: Designer Check — written designer review at any step of a workflow
Description: An optional human review that rides the JOIN between two cards — never a stage of its own, and never blocking. v1 is WRITTEN NOTES, not a call (owner decision 2026-08-30): the designer looks at the artifact on their own time and returns a verdict plus a short note, which attaches to the Library item. Three verdicts only: good to go, change this first, this won't work. Availability is universal (a check is offered after EVERY stage) but the prompting is tiered: loud where a mistake propagates downstream or the next step spends money, quiet everywhere else. The join rules already ship as checkFor() in src/data/studioRouter.ts.
Why: The missing rung on the price ladder. Today it is $19/mo, $49/mo, or a full project costing thousands, with nothing in between — and that gap is where most people stall. It gives the Studio tier a reason to exist that is NOT 'more generations', which is the weakest possible upgrade argument and the one the tiers currently rest on. It is also the studio's real differentiator made visible at the exact moment someone is deciding whether to trust a step, and the warmest sales moment in the business — the designer has just looked at the actual room and the actual layout. Finally it converts the two honest-exit scenarios (mid-renovation, commercial fit-out) from a booking form into a sellable product.
Notes: SCOPE FOR v1 (owner decision 2026-09-01): ADVICE ONLY, and FREE or near-free. The AI-040 wiring that makes advice actionable is a large job, and charging for advice the visitor cannot act on would sell a problem rather than a solution. So v1 is a taste, rationed by a visible queue cap rather than by price - which also removes the whole credit/metering/billing layer from v1. The priced tiers (Free buys one, Design one a month, Studio three a month + same designer + front of queue) turn on WHEN AI-040 LANDS. Trailed on the pricing plans meanwhile as 'Designer review - coming soon'. COPY RULE: say 'a Designature designer' everywhere before submission; reveal the actual person only AFTER assignment, and understate it. NOT an AI feature: a queue + a note + a metered credit. NOTES, NOT A CALL — no scheduling and no calendar coupling, which is roughly 3x the throughput of a call, makes the note itself the deliverable (spoken advice evaporates), and is cheaper to build. The FREE 15-MIN CALL IS UNAFFECTED and stays as the hero CTA and the site-wide Let's Talk primitive. PARKED, not decided: when a call might be mandatory instead of notes — candidate triggers are (1) the verdict is 'this won't work', (2) irreversible decisions out of Plumb/Wire, (3) whole-home or commercial scope, (4) the artifact cannot be judged as it stands; 2-3 are knowable up front while 1 and 4 are only found mid-review, so those would be the designer converting notes into a call, free. Most of the plumbing exists already (saved_items and /api/user/library from AC-002, usage metering, Resend, the admin Consultations tab). NEW: a review_requests table carrying an assignee from day one so it is delegable, an admin queue tab, a credit type, and the connector UI. Tiers differ by how many checks and queue position — never by a stated turnaround, which the studio cannot control. HARD CONSTRAINT: this is the only offering on the board with real marginal cost (the designer's time) — visible capacity, hard queue cap, never unlimited at any price. Spec: _Plan\Website\AI-032v2-Scenario-Pipelines.md

Title: Custom route — describe your situation, get your own pipeline
Description: The escape hatch on the AI-032 v2 router: the visitor describes their situation in their own words and gets an ordered route built from it. Sits LAST in the identity grid, and under every result as a 'this isn't right' link — never as a peer chip, because offered alongside the named scenarios a large share pick free text (it feels more accurate) and we would pay a model call for someone who matched an existing scenario exactly.
Why: Two jobs. (1) It catches everyone the eleven named scenarios do not describe, instead of dead-ending them. (2) It is the research instrument: every description is a scenario nobody has written yet — cluster them, author scenarios 12/13/14 from real customer language, then move those into the deterministic table. The share of traffic taking Custom should FALL over time; that number is the feature's own success metric. It is also a free, continuous source of real customer vocabulary for ad copy and GEO phrase selection.
Notes: The ONE justified model call in the router, and it does not reopen the locked 'the router is not an AI feature' decision, because the job is narrow and checkable. validateCustomRoute() already ships in src/data/studioRouter.ts: the output is validated against explorerRoster.ts and any unknown id dropped (so it can never invent a tool we do not have), de-duplicated, re-sorted into phase order by the same engine as the eleven, capped at 6 steps, and if fewer than 2 valid steps survive it falls through to the free call rather than guessing. REMAINING: the server route, the prompt, and logging the descriptions so they can be clustered.

Title: Apply-and-re-run — designer corrections (and keep/use notes) that reach the prompt
Description: Constraints that reach the AI Vision prompt, from TWO authors. (1) THE DESIGNER, which is the point: a Designer Check verdict of 'change this first' comes back as corrections the tool can consume, and the visitor clicks APPLY AND RE-RUN. The system does the work; the human supplies only the judgement. (2) The visitor: two short capped fields, 'anything that has to stay?' (my piano, the rug) and 'anything you'd like used?' (wooden flooring). Appended as CONSTRAINTS with the structure-preservation instruction placed AFTER them so it always wins.
Why: THIS IS WHAT MAKES DESIGNER CHECK (AI-038) SELLABLE. Without it a designer writes 'move the bed to the long wall' and the visitor has no way to act on it — AI Vision cannot take 'move the bed', it can only regenerate a different room. The advice becomes homework, and the check has sold a problem instead of a solution. That is why AI-038 ships FREE and advice-only until this lands. Separately, the KEEP half is a differentiator on its own: every rival tool deletes the user's things, and nobody solves it.
Notes: REFRAMED 2026-09-01. The original framing was a customer free-text box, and the owner rightly worried we could not produce what people asked for. That risk is real WHEN THE CUSTOMER WRITES THEM — someone types 'add a window'. It is much smaller WHEN THE DESIGNER WRITES THEM, because a designer knows what the tool can do, so the corrections are achievable by construction. Same field, different author, completely different risk profile. Build the designer half FIRST; the customer half is phase 2 and needs the guard below. GUARD for the customer half: a DETERMINISTIC deny-list of structural words (window, wall, door, ceiling, bigger, extend, remove) warning inline 'we keep walls and windows exactly as they are' - no model call needed; a hard character cap against prompt dilution; sanitise for injection (low blast radius - a bad image, not data). ENGINE NOTE: Gemini regenerates the scene so a 'keep' may be ignored; the AI-037 fal FLUX img2img engine keeps the source room and only adds furniture, so it is what makes 'keep my piano' reliable. LATER: promote from the TOOL to the WORKFLOW so constraints also reach Shop My Room and Schedule My Finishes.

Title: Provider cost instrumentation — split Gemini counters + Serper cost-per-run
Description: Make real per-card cost measurable. (a) Split the single `gemini` apiCounter into gemini_image / gemini_vision / gemini_text so a 3.5c image call is distinguishable from a ~0.0001c text call — bumpApiCount sites in server.ts already tag their purpose in comments. (b) Read the existing I-009 serperLog (server.ts ~2213, one row per run with `count`) to derive real searches-per-shopping-list — no new code needed for Serper. (c) Reconcile both against one month of real Gemini + Serper billing.
Why: Every credit price in the Tier Matrix is currently a MODELLED estimate, not a billed figure. R1 (the cost floor) is only as good as the numbers under it — and a wrong estimate on one card is exactly how Shop My Room ended up mispriced at 12 credits. Must land before anything is sold.
Notes: Blocks AI-041 and therefore the whole credit model. Serper half is nearly free — serperLog already records calls per run. Gemini half needs the counter split. Video (Walk My Room) is the shakiest estimate and could move 10x.

Title: Per-tool credit price map + cost-floor guard test
Description: One canonical table mapping each of the 19 roster cards to its credit price, colocated with explorerRoster.ts, plus a vitest asserting no card's cost-per-credit exceeds the ceiling card (Redesign My Room, $0.0035). Test reads the same cost estimates the Tier Matrix uses, so drift fails CI rather than silently leaking margin.
Why: Stops the Shop-My-Room class of bug recurring. A credit price set below its cost floor is invisible in review and unbounded in production — a test is the only thing that catches it when someone adds a tool in a hurry.
Notes: Sheet 'Tier Matrix' section 2 is the source of truth for the numbers; keep them in sync or the test is theatre.

Title: Credit ledger & metering engine
Description: Replace the split generationsLeft / shoppingListsLeft counters with a single server-authoritative credit balance per user. Per-tool debit priced from the AI-041 map, decrement-before-provider-call with bounded refund on failure (same invariant as server/quota.ts today), non-expiring balances for pay-once packs, monthly reset for subscriptions, and a top-up path. No client-callable mutation endpoint.
Why: The whole pricing model rests on this. Today quota is two hardcoded per-feature counters with a lifetime cap; the credit model needs one pool that any of 19 tools can draw on at different rates.
Notes: Must preserve the free-tier lockdown invariant (PR #62): the ONLY way a balance rises is the refund-on-failure path, bounded by the pre-decrement balance. Free tier becomes 50 credits once, replacing 3+3.

Title: Credit packs as one-time purchases on Ameriabank vPOS
Description: Sell Starter $39 / Project $129 / Project Plus $249 as one-time charges on the vPOS rail that already runs the $99 consultation, crediting the balance on verified callback. Includes pack-to-pack upgrade charging only the difference, and top-ups.
Why: Pay-once packs are the only paid product that can be BILLED today — Rail A subscriptions are still blocked after Lemon Squeezy and Paddle both rejected. vPOS one-time payments are shipped and working (I-025).
Notes: Check vPOS handles international cards at $249 and the AMD conversion before promising the price. Subscriptions still need a merchant of record — unrelated blocker.

Title: Rebuild /pricing on the credit model
Description: Port the mockup: three blocks (Free 50 credits · pay-once ladder 400/3,000/6,500 · monthly 1,000/mo), a 'How credits work' band anchoring on 'one render = 10 credits', a 'that's about N redesigns' translation on every card, and the full 19-tool credit price list below the plans.
Why: The live page sells Free / Design $19 / Studio $49, two of which cannot be bought and one of which gates three tools. The credit model removes feature-gating entirely — Free unlocks every tool and is limited by quantity — which also resolves the 'don't call the AI Studio free' framing problem.
Notes: Mockup: _Mockups/Website/WEBSITE-PLAN-pricing-page-credits.html. Copy rules R4 and R5 in Tier Matrix are binding on this page. Also update the Deliverables AI-vs-Studio table in the same PR per the sync rule.

Title: Installable app (PWA) with push notifications. Phase 1 of M-003
Description: Turn the live site into an installable app on iPhone, Android and desktop, then add push. Three build blocks. (1) App manifest, icon set, install prompt and an install page carrying the iPhone Add to Home Screen steps. (2) Service worker and offline shell so the app opens on a weak connection, faster image upload on mobile data, and camera capture straight into AI Vision. (3) Web push: signing keys, subscription storage in Postgres, a notification preferences panel in the account page, quiet hours and one tap off. Owner alerts ship first (credit pack bought, consultation booked, new feedback, failed payment), customer notifications second (your room is ready, credits running low, consultation tomorrow, receipt). No marketing notifications. Feature parity is free: it is the same site, so every desktop page is in the app the day it ships.
Why: Two jobs, both real. It keeps the users we already have, because a home screen icon plus a timely notification is the only reliable way back into a design project that runs for weeks. And it puts a notification on the owner phone the second someone pays or books, which today is only visible by opening the admin page. It will NOT bring new users: there is no store listing to be discovered in. Judge it on retention and on owner response time, never on signups.
Status: Approved (route decided 2026-09-06: PWA with push, not a store wrap, not a native rebuild)
Dependencies: M-001 (mobile UX audit runs first); I-031 credit ledger for the credits low alert; I-025 and I-033 for the payment events behind the owner alerts
Notes: Owner decision 2026-09-06. Chosen over the two alternatives on cost and control: a Capacitor store wrap costs Apple and Google developer accounts, store review and an Apple cut on every in app credit purchase, and a React Native rebuild means every website change gets built twice. THE ONE REAL CATCH: on iPhone, notifications only work after the visitor adds the site to their home screen, so the install prompt copy carries the whole feature and iPhone opt in will lag Android. Scheduled on the weekly board (docs/action-plan.html) as weeks 4 to 9, 2026-09-28 to 2026-11-08, after virtual staging V1. Revisit a real store app only when notification opt in among active users passes roughly half, or when people start asking for it. M-003 stays the destination: the pipeline aware nudges ride on this plumbing once AI-032 v2 defines the pipelines.

Title: Add Farmhouse style. Chip in AI Vision AND a scorable arm of the Style Quiz
Description: Add Farmhouse everywhere a style has to exist, not just as a chip. (a) VISION_STYLES_FULL in src/components/VisionExperience.tsx, plus the STYLE_NAME_TO_PRESET mapping and the STYLE_BRIEFS entry that every chip needs or it silently generates with no style at all (stylePresets.test asserts this). (b) The STYLES array and a STYLE_DESCRIPTIONS entry, summary plus four defining elements, in src/components/StyleQuizScreen.tsx, so the quiz can actually return it as a verdict. (c) The QuizStyle union and image weights in src/data/quizImageWeights.ts, with three or four Farmhouse rooms added to the deck. (d) The ai.style.farmhouse label in LanguageContext for EN, AM and RU. (e) The FAQ answer in src/data/faqs.ts that says 15 curated styles becomes 16.
Why: Farmhouse is one of the highest volume style searches in the US and it is already planned as an article and a Pinterest board in the content calendar batch C. A quiz cannot return a style it does not know, so today a farmhouse leaning visitor gets labelled Rustic, which is the wrong verdict and the wrong shopping list. Cheap to add and it feeds the Pinterest lane.
Dependencies: Owner supplies three or four Farmhouse room images for the quiz deck (Cloudinary)
Notes: Owner request 2026-09-06. The code work is small. The real work is the quiz images, which only the owner can choose. Watch the Rustic overlap: once Farmhouse exists, the Rustic weights in the deck probably need rebalancing or the two will split each other votes. Note the legacy VISION_STYLES array in AIConceptsPage.tsx is deliberately frozen, add to the FULL lists only.
